newsitem.title: USA: Utah lawmaker's ex-husband faces new charges, jail.
newsitem.headline: Utah lawmaker's ex-husband faces new charges, jail.

text.p: Prosecutors said Wednesday that Joseph Waldholtz, the ex-husband of Utah Republican Representative Enid Greene, should be jailed for allegedly using heroin, writing worthless checks and engaging in other criminal acts.

Prosecutors from the U.S. Attorney's Office said bond for the former Republican political operative should be revoked because he allegedly took part in a wide range of criminal conduct since pleading guilty to other charges in June.

"The government alleges that Waldholtz possessed and used heroin, engaged in prescription fraud, stole checks from his stepmother which he then forged with his father's signature and cashed, wrote tens of thousands of dollars of worthless checks and stole credit cards," they said in a statement.
They charged that Waldholtz stole credit cards from his father and a friend and used them for unauthorised purchases.
Chuck Roistacher, an attorney representing Greene, said, "Nothing he does really surprises us in terms of victimising individuals or family members."
He added, "It appears he is incapable of not victimising family members, those who love him. We are surprised about the heroin allegations, but when you think about it, probably we shouldn't be."

An FBI investigation turned up the new allegations. A judge has ordered Waldholtz to appear for a hearing Thursday on the request by prosecutors that he be jailed right away, before sentencing next month on the original criminal charges.
Waldholtz pleaded guilty to four charges in June including filing false federal reports on contributions to Greene's 1994 campaign for Congress. He was her campaign treasurer.

He pleaded guilty to failing to report campaign contributions, making false statements to the federal election agency, causing his then-wife to file a false tax return in 1993 and bank fraud for a check-kiting scheme.
Under federal sentencing guidelines, the 33-year-old Waldholtz could get 18 to 24 months in prison.

At the June hearing, federal judge Norma Holloway Johnson released him on his personal bond, told him to reside with his parents in Pennsylvania, set travel restrictions and ordered him not to commit any new crimes.
Prosecutors charged Waldholtz had violated the judge's order and should be imprisoned immediately. They said the new charges "do not involve in any way Congresswoman Enid Greene."

Greene had been a rising Republican star in Congress until the couple's tangled finances became a major political issue after Waldholtz briefly disappeared late last year. She has maintained he duped her but decided not to seek re-election.
Greene, who won office as a champion of family values, got a divorce on June 5, the same day that Waldholtz pleaded guilty, and has sole custody of their year-old daughter.
Lawyers representing Waldholtz had no comment on the latest charges.
